questions.question: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$. The eigenvalues of $A$ are
questions.note: $A$ is upper triangular, so its eigenvalues are its diagonal entries: $\lambda = 2$ and $\lambda = 2$ (repeated).

questions.question: The value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sin(3x)}{x}$ is
questions.note: Using $\lim_{x\to 0} \dfrac{\sin(kx)}{x} = k$ with $k = 3$, the limit equals $3$.

questions.question: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$. Which of the following statements are TRUE?
questions.note: Row 2 is twice row 1, so the rows are dependent; rows 1 and 3 are not proportional, so $\text{rank}(A) = 2$. By the rank-nullity theorem, $\text{nullity}(A) = 3 - 2 = 1$.

questions.question: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x) = |x|$. Which of the following statements are TRUE?
questions.note: $f$ is continuous everywhere, including at $0$, but has a corner there so it is not differentiable at $x=0$. It is neither injective ($f(-1) = f(1)$) nor surjective onto $\mathbb{R}$ (its range is $[0,\infty)$), so it is not a bijection, and $f(x) \to \infty$ as $|x| \to \infty$, so it is unbounded. Only the first statement is true.

questions.question: The sum of the infinite geometric series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \dfrac{1}{2^n}$ equals _____ (round to two decimal places).
questions.note: This is a geometric series with first term $a = 1/2$ and common ratio $r = 1/2$. The sum is $\dfrac{a}{1-r} = \dfrac{1/2}{1/2} = 1$.

questions.question: Minimize $f(x,y) = x^2 + y^2$ subject to the constraint $x + y = 4$. The minimum value of $f$ is _____.
questions.note: By Lagrange multipliers, $\nabla f = \lambda \nabla g$ gives $2x = \lambda = 2y$, so $x = y$. Combined with $x + y = 4$ this gives $x = y = 2$, so the minimum value is $f(2,2) = 4 + 4 = 8$.
